summary: A short explanation attached to a control, on hover or focus.

pairs.dont: Put something the person needs in order to finish the task in a tooltip.
pairs.do: Put it in the field's hint, where it is always visible.
pairs.why: A tooltip is invisible until you go looking for it, and on touch it may never appear at all.

pairs.dont: Put links, buttons or a form inside a tooltip.
pairs.do: Use a Popover for anything interactive.
pairs.why: A tooltip closes when the pointer leaves, so nothing inside it can reliably be clicked.

pairs.dont: Rely on a tooltip to name an icon-only button.
pairs.do: Give the button an aria-label, and use the tooltip for the extra detail.
pairs.why: A tooltip describes; it does not name. A control with no accessible name is unusable without one.

pairs.do: One sentence, up to about two lines.
pairs.why: It sits over the content the person is reading, and it leaves as soon as they move.

pairs.do: Say what saving will do, or say nothing.
pairs.why: A tooltip that repeats the label teaches people that tooltips are not worth opening.
